structural_note.description: Torah #120 is a short, structurally binary teaching. Its entire argument rests on the contrast between two Sinaitic categories — נַעֲשֶׂה and נִשְׁמַע — and maps each to a mode of Torah engagement (book-learning vs. hearing from the tzaddik). This binary structure means the teaching's full package map is exactly two packages (Package 1: עֲשִׂיָּה/נַעֲשֶׂה cluster; Package 2: נִשְׁמַע cluster), with the Torah's practical instruction serving as the implicit eitza arrow between them. There is no third domain and no uncaptured bechina cluster.
structural_note.good_evil_mirror: Torah #120 does not have a good/evil mirror structure in the conventional sense. Its polarity structure is preserved/lost or empowered/weakened rather than holy/evil. Package 1 (עֲשִׂיָּה/נַעֲשֶׂה) represents the dimension that was 'lost' or 'weakened' at the golden calf — not a demonic force but a structural limitation. Package 2 (נִשְׁמַע) is the preserved crown — the holy path. This asymmetric polarity (neutral vs. good rather than evil vs. good) is consistent with the Torah's tone: it does not condemn books; it explains their post-Calf structural limitation and identifies the path that transcends it.
